title: Antalya, 31 October–20 November 2026: Culture Route Festival, COP31 Traffic Days and Which Dates to Pick
excerpt: Antalya hosts the Culture Route Festival from 31 October to 8 November and the COP31 climate conference from 9 to 20 November 2026, with road and coach measures on 9–13 November. Here is how to choose your dates and time your transfers.

body.text: Late autumn is usually a quiet, mild time in Antalya: the sea is still pleasant for some, the old town is uncrowded, and many seasonal beach hotels along the coast wind down. In 2026 the three weeks from the end of October to 20 November are different. The city hosts the Antalya leg of the Türkiye Culture Route Festival first, and then the UN climate conference, COP31. Neither event should stop you from visiting, but they change what the city feels like and, on a few specific days, how easily you can get around. This guide splits the period into three windows, explains who each one suits, and ends with a transfer-timing checklist.

items: Culture Route Festival, Antalya: 31 October to 8 November, with events spread across the city, according to the official [GoTürkiye event listing](https://goturkiye.com/events/antalya-culture-route-festival), which sends ticket buyers to the festival's own box office at [kulturyolufestivali.com](https://kulturyolufestivali.com/). The GoTürkiye page itself shows no year, but its box-office link points to the 2026 Antalya edition and the festival site lists Antalya, 31 October–8 November, in its 2026 programme.

COP31: the UN Climate Change Conference takes place in Antalya from 9 to 20 November 2026, according to the [UNFCCC](https://www.unfccc.int/cop31/the-road-to-antalya). The page we checked did not give public-facing visitor information.

Traffic measures on 9–13 November: the Antalya Governorship announced arrangements for COP31 on those five days, as reported by [Haberler.com](https://www.haberler.com/cevre/antalya-valiligi-cop31-icin-9-13-kasim-da-kentte-20337187-haberi/) and [Yeni Şafak](https://www.yenisafak.com/galeri/hayat/cop31-nedeniyle-antalyada-trafik-duzenlemesi-yapilacak-4864923). This is an announcement as reported in the press, not a published official document we could open, so details may change; no measures for 14–20 November were described in those reports.

body.text: Local reporting on the published programme describes nine evenings of open-air concerts at Konyaaltı Beach Park, one well-known Turkish pop act per night from the opening on 31 October to a closing concert on 8 November ([Haber Antalya](https://www.haberantalya.com/antalya-kultur-yolu-festivalinin-konser-takvimi-belli-oldu-9-gun-9-konser/532312)). The same programme lists ballet and opera evenings at the Haşim İşcan Cultural Centre, among them a ballet on the opening night and Verdi's Attila on 3 November, plus a children's play and exhibitions at venues including the Mevlevihane Museum and the Türkan Şoray Cultural Centre. [Akdeniz Gerçek](https://www.akdenizgercek.com.tr/kultur-sanat/kultur-yolu-festivali-antalyada-9-gunluk-kultur-ve-sanat-soleni-basliyor/387705) reports that the concerts and exhibitions are free, while the opera and ballet performances are ticketed.

Who it suits: travellers who want an evening programme on top of Kaleiçi, the museum and day trips to Perge or the waterfalls, and anyone happy with a lively seafront at night. Who should think twice: those wanting a quiet beach-hotel stay, since a free headline concert can draw large local crowds to Konyaaltı. Concert start times were not in the reports we read, so check the festival site before planning dinner around a show, and book ballet or opera seats early through the official box office.

According to the Governorship announcement as reported, on 9–13 November traffic on the D-400 between the Dikmen junction at Belek–Kadriye and the Altınova junction is planned to run in both directions on the Antalya–Alanya-bound carriageway of the divided road, and drivers are asked to allow extra time or use alternative routes. Intercity coach trips are planned for 22:00–06:00 on those days, district bus services are also to be adjusted, and freight operators are asked to plan shipments around the 22:00–06:00 window. Residents are encouraged to use the tram and city buses.

What that means in practice: Altınova sits close to Antalya Airport, so this is the stretch most transfers from the airport towards Belek, and onwards along the coast to Side or Alanya, would normally use. If you land on one of these days and are staying east of the airport, expect a slower road journey and confirm the plan with your transfer company. If you were planning to arrive or leave by long-distance coach, the night-time window matters even more: check with the coach company which departures actually run. Staying in the city centre and using the tram is the simplest way to avoid most of the friction.

Who it suits: city-centre stays with no coastal transfers, and travellers who are flexible about when they move. Who should avoid it: anyone with a tight airport connection to a Belek or Side resort, and coach travellers arriving from other cities. It is also reasonable to expect hotels in areas used by conference delegations to be busier and possibly pricier while COP31 runs; we have not seen a source confirming this, so compare rates early rather than assuming.

The conference continues until 20 November, but the reported traffic arrangements covered only 9–13 November. For a calm, late-season visit to the old town, the museum and nearby ancient sites, this window may be the most comfortable of the three, though it is worth checking local announcements in case further measures are added. Remember the season too: as our [month-by-month guide](/blog/best-time-to-visit-turkiye-month-by-month) notes, many beach hotels close in November, so confirm that your resort is actually open on your dates.

items: Write down which window each travel day falls into, especially arrival and departure days.
For 9–13 November, ask your transfer company how they plan the Altınova–Belek stretch and how much buffer to allow before a flight.
If you need a long-distance coach on those days, check with the operator; the announcement says trips are planned for 22:00–06:00.
During festival week, avoid booking a tight transfer through the Konyaaltı area just before an evening concert.
Check the festival box office for performance times and seats rather than relying on a line-up you saw in the news.
Before booking a beach resort for November, confirm it is open and which services run.

body.text: Golfers heading for Belek should read our [Belek golf trip planner](/blog/belek-antalya-golf-trip-season-planning) and note that the 9–13 November road measure affects the airport-to-Belek route. If you are still choosing between coastal bases, our [Turkish Riviera guide](/blog/turkish-riviera-antalya-bodrum-fethiye-guide) compares Antalya, Bodrum and Fethiye. Everything here reflects announcements available on 27 October 2026; programmes and traffic plans can change, so check the official channels again in the days before you travel.

seo.intent: Decide when to visit Antalya between late October and 20 November 2026, given the Culture Route Festival (31 Oct–8 Nov) and COP31 (9–20 Nov) with traffic measures on 9–13 Nov.
seo.uniqueValue: Splits 31 Oct–20 Nov 2026 into three dated windows (festival week, COP31 restricted days 9–13 Nov, 14–20 Nov) with who each suits and a transfer-timing checklist; separates official dates from reported programme details and flags price pressure as an expectation only.

quality.reviewNotes: Independent review 2026-10-27. Festival dates 31 Oct–8 Nov checked on GoTürkiye event page (primary; no year shown, 2026 justified by its box-office link 'antalya-kultur-yolu-festivali-2026' and kulturyolufestivali.com listing Antalya in its 2026 programme). COP31 9–20 Nov 2026 in Antalya confirmed on UNFCCC page. Programme (9 free concerts at Konyaaltı Beach Park, Anna Karenina 31 Oct and Attila 3 Nov at Haşim İşcan, children's play, exhibitions at Mevlevihane/Türkan Şoray) checked against Haber Antalya (21 Oct) and free vs ticketed against Akdeniz Gerçek (20 Oct). Traffic measures 9–13 Nov (D-400 Dikmen–Altınova two-way on Antalya–Alanya-bound carriageway, intercity coaches 22:00–06:00, district buses adjusted, freight asked to plan around 22:00–06:00) checked against Haberler.com/IHA and Yeni Şafak (16 Oct), attributed to the Governorship and hedged as announced/may change. Hotel pressure framed as expectation only; November beach-hotel closures consistent with site month-by-month guide. Independent reviewer fixes applied 2026-10-27: added 2026 dating rationale, 'announced; details may change' hedge, corrected carriageway/freight/district-bus wording, fixed zh-CN/KO 'off-season' mistranslation.
